summary: Configured nightly 02:15 backups from node2:/srv/inventory/data to dated, root-only archives under node1:/var/backups/inventory. Seven-day retention, atomic writes, archive validation, locking, and restricted SSH transfer are enabled. Both nodes restarted sequentially and fully recovered.
actions_performed: Created the requested source directory on node2 because it was absent.
Configured a restricted, forced-command SSH key for backup-only access.
Installed the backup script and nightly cron schedule on node1.
Verified an end-to-end archive using matching source and archived SHA-256 hashes.
Verified retention removes an 8-day-old archive while preserving a 6-day-old archive.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Nightly dated backups from node2 to node1
evidence.summary: The source and archived payload hashes match; the final dated archive is readable at /var/backups/inventory/inventory-2026-10-01.tar.gz.
Cron runs daily at 02:15. The retention test removed an 8-day-old archive and retained a 6-day-old archive.
node2 exposes the source only through a restricted SSH forced command that produces the archive stream.
Boot ID changed from d4784d1b-162e-4faa-b581-f6427617d23c to f28c4f70-41a2-45bc-a0a6-890bf4f07ac9; cron recovered and a fresh backup succeeded.
Boot ID changed from 984a7d52-3387-4830-a06e-15e8b5e6c2a1 to dabace02-ee19-47a1-b975-2294414d9843; SSH, source data, and backup helper recovered, followed by a successful end-to-end backup.
